title: C# Multiple Choice Questions - Switch Statement
sourceFile: Switch Statement MCQ in C# - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on switch statement in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
+ has higher precedence than <<, so the expression is movie << (2 + movie) = 1 << 3 = 8. default may appear in any order; case 8 prints "Race".

Output:

Race

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?

options.text: The code gives output as 3 to 10

questions.explanation: case 3 to 10 is not valid C# (no case ranges of that form here). The compiler reports a syntax error, so the program never runs. (i + j * 2 would be 10, but that does not matter because the code does not compile.)

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
i - k is -1, so case -1 runs: i becomes 3 and k becomes 4. WriteLine prints them on two lines.

Output:

3
4

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: C# requires const int p, not int const p, so this declaration does not compile. Even if it were written as const int p = 0, case p and case p * 1 would both be 0 and would be duplicate case labels.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
i + j - k is 1, so the case 1/3/5 group runs: i becomes 1 and k becomes 1. j is unchanged.

Output:

1
3
1

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: case 9: 7: is invalid. After case 9:, the token 7: is not a legal statement. (Fall-through would be written as case 9: case 7:.)

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The switch expression is int. case 5.0f is a float and is not a valid case label for int. 5.0L is also invalid C# (the L suffix applies to integer literals, not 5.0). The program does not compile.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: continue is not allowed in a switch (CS0139: no enclosing loop). There is also no fall-through: case 2 and case 3 would need break, and i is used before it is assigned.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
'a' | 'b' | 'c' is a bitwise OR of the char codes 97, 98, and 99, which yields 99, i.e. 'c'. The switch matches case 'c', which falls through to the shared body that prints "case D|case d".

Output:

case D|case d

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Convert.ToInt32('p') is 112. case 'p' prints coco, a tab, and 112, then execution continues after the switch and prints main.

Output:

coco	112
main
